method: Official pages reviewed in the research conversation; relevant AOK source files inspected at the baseline commit. Summaries are paraphrases, not mirrored articles.
runtimeVerification: No model inference, migration campaign, native Goal lifecycle, sandbox enforcement or multi-agent execution was tested.

sources.title: Using PLANS.md for multi-hour problem solving
sources.supports: A self-contained living plan can preserve progress, decisions, acceptance and recovery for complex work. ExecPlan is a repository-defined convention.
sources.limitations: The page is marked archived; do not adopt its historical model recommendation or treat PLANS.md as an execution engine.

sources.title: Harness engineering
sources.supports: Repository navigation, enforceable boundaries, observable applications and maintained knowledge improve agent execution.
sources.limitations: A particular team experiment; its throughput and autonomy are not guarantees for other repositories.

sources.title: Custom Code Review rules for Codex
sources.supports: Scoped AGENTS.md review rules can encode consequential invariants and safe alternatives; evaluate violations and safe counterexamples.
sources.limitations: Additional review guidance does not replace tests, required approvals or branch protection.

sources.title: Maintaining software with the GPT-6 family
sources.supports: Gather evidence for maintenance candidates, prioritize benefit, start small and expand after review; feed findings into the next prompt.
sources.limitations: Reported results and model comparisons are specific to the described work and were not reproduced here.

sources.title: Migrate a Legacy Codebase with Sandbox Agents
sources.supports: Keep trusted orchestration outside isolated task workspaces; validate returned patches and typed reports; stage and verify each migration unit.
sources.limitations: The demonstrated host/sandbox architecture is one deployment pattern, not an AOK capability or a universal sandbox security guarantee.

sources.title: Iterating Development Workflows with Codex
sources.supports: Separate goals, plans, phase context, build evidence and review ownership; use observed friction to improve procedures and forward-test them.
sources.limitations: The extra files and directory names are optional conventions. Example approval policies must be reconciled with the actual user authorization and project policy.

sources.title: Using Goals in Codex
sources.supports: Goals are durable thread-scoped objectives with evidence-based completion, continuation controls and budget accounting.
sources.limitations: Native thread state is distinct from repository files, schedules and permissions. AOK has no native Goal adapter in this snapshot.

sources.title: Best practices for Claude Code
sources.supports: Explore and plan when uncertainty warrants it; provide executable verification and specific context; use direct execution for small clear edits.
sources.limitations: Recommendations require task-specific judgment; the article is not a requirement for a new approval before every authorized edit.

sources.title: Common workflows
sources.supports: Recipes cover exploration, debugging, refactoring, testing, documentation, PRs, session resumption, worktrees and scripted use.
sources.limitations: Examples are tool-specific and do not establish that AOK renders or executes them.

sources.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
sources.supports: Initialization and incremental coding sessions use startup instructions, feature state, progress notes and Git history for continuity.
sources.limitations: One experimental pattern, initially focused on full-stack application development; it does not prove multiple agents always outperform one.

sources.title: Harness design for long-running application development
sources.supports: A separate evaluator can exercise a running app; calibrate its judgment and remove scaffolding that no longer improves outcomes.
sources.limitations: Evaluation is not infallible; examples show overhead and model-specific tradeoffs rather than a universal quality guarantee.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.supports: Choose simple solutions first; prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator/worker and evaluator loops fit different task structures.
sources.limitations: Architecture patterns are options rather than a mandate to use an SDK, multiple agents or adaptive execution.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.supports: Treat context as finite; retrieve relevant information and preserve useful state through compaction, notes and appropriate separation.
sources.limitations: Long context is not equivalent to reliable retrieval, and notes are not authoritative evidence without provenance.

sources.title: Keep Claude working toward a goal
sources.supports: A session-scoped /goal uses a separate evaluator after turns and has documented automatic clearing and stopping conditions.
sources.limitations: Do not assume Codex Goal persistence, lifecycle or pause semantics; a goal does not change permissions.

sources.title: Orchestrate subagents at scale with dynamic workflows
sources.supports: A JavaScript script can codify orchestration of many subagents, with documented run management and resumption behavior.
sources.limitations: Feature availability and runtime behavior are vendor-specific; separate contexts do not imply isolated shared resources.

sources.title: How Anthropic runs large-scale code migrations with Claude Code
sources.supports: Build a behavioral judge, stress-test translation rules, use resumable units, classify repeated failures and verify old/new parity.
sources.limitations: A unit being translated or an output file existing is not campaign acceptance; compatibility and integration still need evidence.
